newsitem.title: TURKMENISTAN: Turkmenistan Caspian oil, gas tender set for Sep 1.
newsitem.headline: Turkmenistan Caspian oil, gas tender set for Sep 1.

text.p: Turkmenistan will open the first round of an international tender for developing oil and gas deposits on the shelf the Caspian Sea on September 1, President Saparmurat Niyasov said on Thursday.
In an official resolution, obtained by Reuters, Niyazov said bids would be accepted until November 28 and the results of the tender would be announced by January 1, 1998.
U.S. Western Atlas International estimates Turkmen's Caspian shelf resources are 3.0 billion tonnes of oil and 4.5 trillion cubic meters of natural gas.
The winner of the tender will have various options on how to work with Turmenistan, ranging from setting up interntional consortiums to production-sharing agreements.
Turkmenistan will hold presentations for the tender in Ashgabat, Vienna, London and Huston in September and November this year.
The regulation said foreign investors would receive geological, geophysical and technical information about the Turkmen shelf area, prepared by Britain's Robertson Research.
Deputy Oil and Gas Minister Khoshgeldy Babayev said Western Atlas was now carrying out seismic research in the shallow waters of the Caspian Sea.
"This territory is the most interesting one from the point of view of discovering big hydrocabon deposits," he said.
Test well drilling in the area will start in December this year.
Shell, Mobil Corp, Unocal, Amoco Corp, Exxon, Agip Spa, Japan National Oil Corp, Turkish Petroleum Company and the Iranian Oil Ministry bought seismic data on the area of the Caspian.
